title: Elodie and the Thorn
premise: Zephyrine Nystrom, last of the oath-bound swordspeakers, smuggles contraband through the Thornfell mountains until a prophecy written a century ago names tonight's date and drags them into its fulfillment. Bound by oath to a prophecy they never chose, Zephyrine must escort Elodie Vasse, a runaway heir carrying the last living dragon-fire, to the door of Vaelthorne—a country erased from maps and memory a hundred years past. Hunted by the Ashen Court, which erased Vaelthorne to seize its fire, they gather a found family of exiles, heretics, and one very old cartographer who remembers what the world forgot. At the door, Zephyrine learns the price: the oath demands a swordspeaker's life to reopen what was closed. In the end, Elodie refuses the sacrifice, shatters the prophecy itself, and the found family carries Vaelthorne's fire not back to a dead country but forward, founding a new one from the ashes of the old.
about_author: Dominic Eastwick is the pen name of a former mountain guide who spent a decade leading expeditions through ranges that appear on no modern map. Their fiction blends cartographic obsession with a deep suspicion of inherited duty.

chapters.title: The Date in the Margins
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Smuggling moonsteel through the Thornfell passes, Zephyrine pauses at a roadside shrine and finds a century-old prophecy book whose margins name tonight's date—and their own name. The emotional beat is dread: a life built on choosing one's own roads suddenly has an author.

chapters.title: A Passenger with Fire in Her Blood
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. A desperate woman, Elodie Vasse, hires passage east, hiding a coal of living dragon-fire beneath her skin that burns anyone who touches her. Zephyrine recognizes the prophecy's second figure and takes the job anyway. Beat: reluctant responsibility hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Ashen Court's Writ
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Pursuers arrive—a magistrate of the Ashen Court bearing a writ declaring Elodie stolen property of a country that no longer exists. A rooftop escape through a burning market town. Beat: Elodie's first taste of being hunted for what she carries rather than who she is.

chapters.title: The Cartographer Who Remembers
chapters.summary: Dual POV. They seek Old Brammel, a cartographer exiled for mapping Vaelthorne, whose memory the Ashen Court tried to burn out of the world. He confirms the prophecy and the location of the door. Beat: the comfort of being believed after years of solitary certainty.

chapters.title: Oath and Anchor
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. The swordspeaker's oath activates fully: Zephyrine can no longer abandon Elodie, feeling her pain as their own. They resent the chain even as it deepens their bond. Beat: the bitter discovery that duty and affection are not the same thing.

chapters.title: The Salt Road Ambush
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. The Ashen Court's knights ambush them on the salt road. Brammel is wounded; Zephyrine's blade speaks for the first time in years, singing words of the old tongue. Beat: Elodie sees the cost of Zephyrine's power—each word spoken ages them.

chapters.title: The Heretic's Hearth
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Shelter with a hidden community of Vaelthorne expatriates who keep forbidden hearth-songs alive. Elodie is welcomed as kin; Zephyrine, an outsider to their own oath's homeland, watches from the doorway. Beat: longing for a family that fits.

chapters.title: What the Fire Shows
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. The dragon-fire shows Elodie visions of Vaelthorne's fall—and reveals her grandmother gave her the coal knowingly, a deliberate inheritance. Beat: rage at being made a vessel, then grief, then a fierce decision to carry it on her own terms.

chapters.title: The Knight Who Knelt
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Ser Aldous, the Ashen knight who led the ambush, defects, unable to keep hunting a child for a crime committed before her birth. The group distrusts him. Beat: the fragile, dangerous arithmetic of forgiveness.

chapters.title: Crossing the Unmapped
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. The company enters territory the Ashen Court literally erased—blank on every map, where roads loop and stars are wrong. Only Zephyrine's swordspeaker senses and Brammel's half-burned memory can navigate. Beat: trust tested to breaking in the featureless dark.

chapters.title: The Price of a Word
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Zephyrine collapses from the toll of spoken power. Elodie tends them and learns the full terms of the oath: the door of Vaelthorne opens only for a swordspeaker's life freely given. Beat: horror, and the first lie Elodie tells to keep hope alive.

chapters.title: The Court of Ash and Ledger
chapters.summary: Ser Aldous's POV. Flashback to the Ashen Court's founding: clerks who burned a country into a ledger-line and called it order. Aldous reveals the Court is marching on the door. Beat: the banality of institutional evil, and one man's quiet mutiny.

chapters.title: Hearth-Song in the Dark
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Trapped in a collapsed pass, the company survives by singing the Vaelthorne hearth-songs; the fire answers, lighting their way. Zephyrine finally sings too. Beat: the found family becomes real—not by declaration but by shared song in a dark place.

chapters.title: The Traitor's Toll
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. A guide they trusted sells their route to the Court. Brammel dies holding the pass so the others can flee, pressing his half-finished map of Vaelthorne into Elodie's hands. Beat: grief braided with inheritance—she now carries the fire and the map and the memory.

chapters.title: The Door That Was a Promise
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. They reach the door: a plain stone arch in a valley of ash, inscribed with the first words of the swordspeaker's oath. Zephyrine understands at last why the prophecy chose them. Beat: grim acceptance, and quiet farewell preparations Elodie pretends not to see.

chapters.title: The Ashen Court Arrives
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The Court's army descends, led by the Lord Registrar who erased Vaelthorne and now wants its fire as his final entry. A battle at the arch. Beat: everything the found family has built is tested at once.

chapters.title: Swordsong
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Zephyrine speaks the full swordsong, aging decades in a dozen lines, cutting the Registrar's host apart and holding the arch. Beat: triumph and ruin in the same breath—the oath's price coming due.

chapters.title: The Refusal
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. At the threshold, Zephyrine prepares to die; Elodie instead drives the dragon-fire into the prophecy book itself, burning the words that demanded a sacrifice. The door opens not for a death but for a choice. Beat: defiance of fate as the true inheritance.

chapters.title: A Country Made of People
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Vaelthorne is gone—but its hearths, songs, and exiles are not. The company chooses to found a new holding in the Thornfell valleys, with the arch as its gate. Beat: mourning transmuted into building.

chapters.title: The Last Entry
chapters.summary: Ser Aldous's POV. Aldous delivers the Registrar's ledger to the new settlement and burns it page by page, keeping only one line: names of the dead, read aloud. Beat: accountability as a form of peace.

chapters.title: What Zephyrine Kept
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Old before their time, Zephyrine trains a new generation of swordspeakers—oath rewritten, freely sworn, no life demanded. Elodie tends the fire at the hearth. Beat: the price of survival paid in years, repaid in purpose.

chapters.title: Elodie and the Thorn
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV, years later. Elodie leads a caravan through the passes, past the shrine where a prophecy book still lies open to a blank final page. A young traveler asks about the scarred old swordspeaker by the fire. Beat: the story becoming a hearth-song itself—found family as the country that endures.
